name: table
title: Table
description: Invoices, transaction histories, and small collections of structured records.
docs:
## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/table ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | table | `@components/cadence/table/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/table.json) | [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: table](https://cadence.dev/r/table.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. Copy both target files, keeping `table/index.tsx` and `lib/cn.ts` in the same `cadence/` tree so the relative import resolves. Preserve the source's `"use client"` directive. Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. Table needs no motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS; all three motion modes keep its native table parts static. Row colour feedback is CSS state feedback. Usage, Footer totals, Density and alignment, Horizontal overflow, and Empty results pass serializable props and children and can be composed in a Server Component. Selected rows and Row actions require a client caller for their state and event handlers. Refs and event handlers also require a client caller. Row actions additionally uses [Button](/components/button): install it separately, or copy every target and recursive dependency from its Manual panel, including its motion setup. The other examples and the top preview need no additional component dependencies. Keep the native caption, header, body and footer hierarchy, provide a meaningful caption or accessible name, and set header `scope` as shown below. Table does not fetch records, calculate totals, sort, filter, paginate or own selection. The caller supplies stable row keys, data, selected state and action handlers; `data-state="selected"` only styles a row. Controls inside cells keep their own keyboard behaviour. Table's props, classes and ref target the `table`, not its automatic `overflow-x-auto` wrapper. Constrain the surrounding layout with `min-w-0` where needed, and choose column widths and wrapping yourself. For a wide table, supply `tabIndex={0}`, a caption and a visible focus ring as in Horizontal overflow, then verify native arrow-key scrolling in your target browsers. Columns remain present; Table adds no grid keyboard model. ## Usage ```tsx import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; export function Invoices() { return ( Recent invoices. Invoice Amount INV-001 $250.00
); } ``` ## Footer totals `TableFooter` renders a native `tfoot`. This example keeps a row header, spans the label across two columns and aligns the total with the amounts. The caller supplies both the records and the total; Table does no arithmetic. ```tsx import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableFooter, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; const invoices = [ { id: "INV-001", status: "Paid", method: "Credit card", amount: "$250.00" }, { id: "INV-002", status: "Pending", method: "Bank transfer", amount: "$150.00" }, { id: "INV-003", status: "Unpaid", method: "PayPal", amount: "$350.00" }, ]; export function FooterTotalsExample() { return ( November invoice totals. Invoice Status Amount {invoices.map((invoice) => ( {invoice.id} {invoice.status} {invoice.amount} ))} Total $750.00
); } ``` ## Selected rows Selection belongs to the application. These named native checkboxes own their checked state and set `data-state="selected"` on the corresponding rows. The attribute only adds row colour: it does not turn a row into a control, add `aria-selected`, or introduce grid navigation. Space toggles the focused checkbox; the initial selection is independent of every other specimen. ```tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; const invoices = [ { id: "INV-001", status: "Paid", method: "Credit card", amount: "$250.00" }, { id: "INV-002", status: "Pending", method: "Bank transfer", amount: "$150.00" }, { id: "INV-003", status: "Unpaid", method: "PayPal", amount: "$350.00" }, ]; export function SelectedRowsExample() { const [selected, setSelected] = useState(["INV-001"]); return (
Choose invoices for your report. Include Invoice Amount {invoices.map((invoice) => ( setSelected((current) => event.target.checked ? [...current, invoice.id] : current.filter((id) => id !== invoice.id), ) } className="size-4 accent-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring" /> {invoice.id} {invoice.amount} ))}

Selected invoices: {selected.length}

); } ``` ## Density and alignment Table has no size or density prop. Compare the default spacing with caller-supplied compact cell padding and header height. Left-aligned labels, centred counts and right-aligned amounts are fixed in both tables; `tabular-nums` helps compare numbers. These are CSS choices, not component variants. ```tsx import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; export function DensityAlignmentExample() { return (
{[false, true].map((compact) => ( {compact ? "Compact spacing" : "Default spacing"} with numeric alignment. Plan Seats Monthly Team 12 $240.00
))}
); } ``` ## Row actions Links and buttons inside cells keep their own keyboard behaviour. Tab reaches the invoice history link and then the payment action; Enter or Space activates the button. The local handler changes only this example and disables the completed action. In an application, the caller owns persistence, pending state and errors. Install `@cadence/button` alongside Table for this composition; the button inherits the surrounding motion settings. ```tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; export function RowActionsExample() { const [paid, setPaid] = useState(false); return (
Invoice actions owned by the application. Invoice Status Action INV-001 history {paid ? "Paid" : "Pending"}

{paid ? "INV-001 marked paid locally." : "No payment action yet."}

); } ``` ## Horizontal overflow The built-in container scrolls when the table needs more room. Constrain the surrounding layout with `min-w-0`; put the minimum width and a visible focus ring on Table itself. In this wide specimen, focus the named table and press horizontal arrow keys to scroll its ancestor. No columns are removed, and there is no grid arrow-key selection model. Check keyboard scrolling in your target browsers. ```tsx import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; export function HorizontalOverflowExample() { return ( Delivery records. Focus the table and use horizontal arrow keys to scroll. Invoice Customer Delivery reference Amount INV-001 morgan@example.com November workspace delivery $250.00
); } ``` ## Empty results Keep the header relationships and place the empty message in one cell spanning every column. The caller decides that the result is empty and provides the message; Table does not fetch or filter records. `whitespace-normal` lets this message wrap at narrow widths. ```tsx import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; export function EmptyResultsExample() { return ( Invoices matching the application's current query. Invoice Status Amount No matching invoices. Try another query in your application.
); } ``` ## When to use - Invoice summaries with amounts and payment states. - Transaction histories with a few consistent columns. - Small record collections where column comparisons matter. ## When not to use - For page layout: use CSS grid or flex. - For large collections needing sorting, filtering, pagination, or virtualization: compose those behaviours in the application; Table only supplies markup and styles. - For independent summaries with no column relationships: use cards or a list. ## API All eight exports accept `React.ComponentProps` for their native element, including `children`, `className`, `style`, event handlers, ARIA attributes and React 19 `ref`. Classes merge last. No custom props or defaults are added. | Export | Element | | --- | --- | | `Table` | `table` | | `TableHeader` | `thead` | | `TableBody` | `tbody` | | `TableFooter` | `tfoot` | | `TableRow` | `tr` | | `TableHead` | `th` | | `TableCell` | `td` | | `TableCaption` | `caption` | Each part's slot is its kebab-case name: `table`, `table-header`, `table-body`, `table-footer`, `table-row`, `table-head`, `table-cell`, and `table-caption`. `Table` also creates a `div` with `data-slot="table-container"` and `relative w-full overflow-x-auto`. Its props, classes and ref target the **table**, not that wrapper. Size the surrounding layout to constrain the scrolling region. `TableHead` and `TableCell` keep upstream's no-wrap and checkbox alignment styles. Rows retain hover, `data-state="selected"` and descendant `aria-expanded` feedback. ## Motion contract T0: no motion recipe, hook, provider, or animation runtime. All modes render the same static table. Row colour feedback is the upstream CSS colour transition; rows do not enter, reorder, resize, or animate selection. | Mode | Animated properties | | --- | --- | | full | none | | reduced | none | | none | none | No timing token or interruption lifecycle applies. ## Accessibility - Native table, row, header, cell and caption semantics remain intact. Provide a meaningful caption or an accessible name and use `scope` for header relationships. - Static rows and cells stay out of the tab order. Links, buttons and checkboxes inside cells keep their native keyboard interaction; no grid arrow-key model is added. - The wrapper scrolls horizontally on narrow screens; columns are not removed. If keyboard scrolling needs an explicit focus stop across your target browsers, pass `tabIndex={0}` to the named table with a visible focus ring, as in Usage. This supplies a focusable descendant of the scrolling container; arrow keys can scroll that ancestor without adding grid keyboard semantics. - No layout measurement or data processing runs. Render large datasets through application-owned pagination or virtualization; the server markup remains native HTML. ## Responsiveness and performance The table fills its container, which provides native horizontal scrolling when columns need more width. The caller owns column sizing, wrapping and any sticky behavior. Rows are all rendered; large datasets need application pagination or virtualization. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Preserve the table hierarchy: caption, header, body and footer belong inside Table. - Class names and refs on Table address the table; constrain its parent for overflow. - Table does not fetch data, validate values, sort, filter, paginate or own selection. - Do not add decorative row entrance or reorder motion to this T0 component.
